text:
THE EVIDENCE™
WELCOME TO KINDERGARTEN, AMERICA
James Talarico Asks What Would Happen If We Ran the World Like a Kindergarten Classroom. Perhaps We Should Take Him Seriously.

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

Texas Democratic politician James Talarico has offered America a remarkable thought experiment: “What if we ran our world like we run a kindergarten classroom? Because at the end of the day, aren't we all just really big kindergartners?” Those words, captured in a video dated May 27, 2020, resurfaced in September 2026 as Talarico pursued a seat in the United States Senate. The quotation is authentic, although the nine-second clip does not establish that he was advocating a literal kindergarten system of government. His background as a former public-school teacher suggests he may have been appealing to familiar classroom virtues such as sharing, compassion, cooperation, and mutual respect. Nevertheless, when a politician proposes an analogy between governing the world and supervising five-year-olds, the comparison deserves considerably more examination than an approving smile and a round of applause.

Suppose we actually accepted the premise. Suppose we reorganized government, diplomacy, criminal justice, national defense, and the American economy around the operating principles of a kindergarten classroom. What would this magnificent new civilization look like? Would international conflicts disappear because everyone learned to use their inside voices? Would violent criminals reconsider their careers after spending twenty minutes in the reflection corner? Would the national debt vanish if Congress learned to share its crayons? And who, exactly, would be the teacher supervising 340 million oversized kindergarten students?

It is an intriguing concept, particularly when we consider that Washington already resembles a dysfunctional kindergarten classroom in which the children have access to nuclear weapons, taxpayer money, government credit cards, and the authority to issue subpoenas. The difference is that ordinary kindergarten students generally demonstrate some capacity to learn from their mistakes. Washington has been repeating many of the same ones for generations, frequently rewarding the responsible parties with reelection, promotions, lucrative consulting contracts, and television appearances explaining why everyone else is responsible.

Under the new kindergarten government, the first order of business would undoubtedly be congressional reform. The House of Representatives would become the House of Sharing, the Senate would be transformed into the Circle of Friends, and the Speaker of the House would be replaced by a designated classroom helper responsible for passing out juice boxes and ensuring that nobody monopolized the crayons. Congressional hearings would begin with elected representatives sitting cross-legged on a colorful carpet while the presiding teacher reminded everyone that interrupting is rude, name-calling hurts people's feelings, and taking something that belongs to somebody else requires permission. The last rule would create immediate difficulties for the tax-writing committees, which would presumably request an exemption on the grounds that taking other people's money is not stealing when the government does it.

Consider how this system would handle a congressional investigation. A witness accused of fraud, corruption, or deliberately misleading the public would be invited to discuss the importance of honesty. If the witness refused to answer questions, the committee would explain that cooperation makes everyone happier. Should the witness continue refusing, the matter would be escalated to the reflection corner, where the offender would remain until demonstrating an improved attitude. Members of Congress found to have misrepresented facts would receive a similar opportunity for personal growth, although the resulting demand for reflection corners would probably necessitate a substantial expansion of the Capitol complex. The Congressional Budget Office would estimate the cost at $18 billion, which Congress would immediately approve as an essential investment in emotional wellness.

The federal budget would present another fascinating opportunity for childhood education. Instead of complicated appropriations bills containing thousands of pages of expenditures that few legislators have actually read, Congress would receive construction paper, paste, scissors, and a collection of colorful stickers. Members would be instructed to place a green sticker next to programs the country could afford and a red sticker next to programs requiring borrowed money. Unfortunately, nearly everything would receive a red sticker, creating an immediate shortage that the Federal Reserve would resolve by printing additional stickers. When someone suggested that the government could not continue spending beyond its means indefinitely, the classroom supervisor would explain that negative comments undermine group morale and that everyone should concentrate on finding solutions rather than assigning blame. The national debt would continue expanding, but at least the charts would be colorful.

Foreign policy would become considerably more entertaining. Imagine the United Nations operating under the same rules used to settle disputes over playground equipment. Russia would be reminded that taking another country's territory without permission violates the sharing agreement. China would receive a laminated certificate explaining that other people's property belongs to them, even when those other people are considerably smaller. Iran would be encouraged to explore its frustrations through finger painting rather than military threats, while North Korea would be advised that threatening classmates with nuclear annihilation is unacceptable behavior. Diplomatic negotiations would conclude with everyone joining hands, singing about friendship, and promising to make better choices tomorrow. Unfortunately, when tomorrow arrived and someone invaded another country, the international community would have little choice but to impose the ultimate kindergarten sanction: suspension of recess privileges.

The Pentagon would also require extensive restructuring. Generals would be replaced by certified conflict-resolution specialists, aircraft carriers would become floating friendship centers, and military exercises would focus on teaching adversaries to recognize and respect one another's feelings. Nuclear deterrence would be replaced by an escalating system of behavioral warnings. A hostile government threatening the United States would receive an official reminder about kindness. A second threat would generate a strongly worded letter expressing disappointment. An actual military attack would trigger an emergency meeting to determine whether the aggressor was experiencing emotional distress or had simply failed to receive sufficient positive reinforcement during childhood. By the time the committee completed its findings, the Pentagon might already be occupied by enemy forces, although the invaders would undoubtedly appreciate the complimentary refreshments.

There is, of course, a reason the adult world does not operate according to kindergarten rules. Five-year-olds are generally learning how to control impulses, manage frustration, respect boundaries, and understand the consequences of their actions. Their disputes usually involve toys, playground privileges, classroom activities, and relatively minor disagreements. Adult political leaders, military commanders, organized criminals, and dictators frequently understand consequences perfectly well. They may simply calculate that aggression, dishonesty, coercion, or violence will produce the outcomes they desire. Treating deliberate exploitation as a misunderstanding to be resolved through reassurance is not compassion. It is a potentially catastrophic failure to distinguish immaturity from calculated misconduct.

Our criminal justice system would provide perhaps the most revealing demonstration of this philosophy. Imagine a courtroom in which the judge exchanged traditional judicial robes for a colorful cardigan and began each proceeding by asking whether everyone was having a good day. Armed robbery would be classified as an inappropriate sharing decision, assault would become an unsuccessful attempt at emotional communication, and repeat offenses would indicate that the defendant required additional encouragement. A convicted criminal would be asked to explain why taking another person's property or inflicting bodily injury was unkind. The sentence would consist of a written apology, a period of supervised reflection, and a commitment to making better choices. Victims might reasonably object that the offender had already received multiple opportunities to improve, but such negativity would threaten the supportive learning environment.

The problem becomes considerably more serious when we recognize the difference between teaching children responsibility and excusing adults from responsibility. A child who strikes a classmate may genuinely lack the emotional maturity to understand the full consequences of the act. An adult who deliberately assaults another person cannot automatically claim the same deficiency. A civilized justice system should recognize rehabilitation as a legitimate objective, but it must also recognize deterrence, accountability, proportional punishment, and the protection of innocent people. Those principles cannot simply be replaced with therapeutic language without imposing substantial risks on the people government is supposed to protect.

The economy would undergo an equally impressive transformation. Competition would be discouraged because someone inevitably loses, and losing can damage self-esteem. Businesses would be evaluated primarily according to whether everyone felt included, respected, and emotionally supported. Companies generating profits would be reminded that sharing is important, while businesses losing money would receive participation awards acknowledging their contributions to the classroom. Bankruptcy would become an unexpected learning experience, unemployment would be renamed an opportunity for personal exploration, and inflation would be explained as a temporary disagreement between prices and purchasing power. Anyone insisting that goods and services must actually be produced before they can be consumed would be accused of failing to appreciate the emotional dimensions of economic activity.

Unfortunately, the American economy is not a classroom exercise. Farmers must grow food, truckers must deliver merchandise, engineers must design functioning infrastructure, electricians must maintain power systems, and businesses must generate sufficient revenue to cover their expenses. A hospital cannot operate indefinitely on positive affirmations, and a trucking company cannot purchase diesel fuel by presenting the attendant with a gold star. Economic production requires competence, discipline, capital, risk-taking, accountability, and the willingness to acknowledge failure when something does not work. These are adult responsibilities with measurable consequences. Pretending otherwise would not eliminate economic reality; it would merely postpone the moment when reality delivered the bill.

But perhaps the most consequential aspect of the kindergarten analogy concerns the relationship between government and the governed. A kindergarten classroom is an inherently authoritarian environment, although that authority is ordinarily exercised for the protection and development of children. The teacher establishes the schedule, controls classroom activities, determines when students may eat, supervises their movements, sets behavioral expectations, and imposes consequences for misconduct. Children do not negotiate constitutional limitations on classroom authority because they are not yet equipped to exercise full adult independence. They are supervised precisely because their judgment remains under development.

Now consider what happens when that arrangement becomes the model for governing adults. Somebody must assume the role of teacher, and everybody else becomes a student. Somebody decides which activities are permissible, which opinions are acceptable, what constitutes inappropriate conduct, and how much independence the population can safely exercise. Government becomes the parent, bureaucracy becomes the classroom administration, and citizens are expected to follow instructions while being reassured that every restriction is imposed for their own good.

That is an extraordinarily dangerous foundation for a constitutional republic. The American system does not begin with the assumption that citizens are children who must earn permission to exercise their freedom. It begins with individual rights and a government whose legitimate powers are delegated and limited. The First Amendment does not require citizens to raise their hands before expressing unpopular opinions. The Fourth Amendment does not permit government agents to inspect personal property merely because the classroom supervisor suspects misbehavior. Due process cannot be suspended simply because an official believes punishment would promote a healthier social environment. The Bill of Rights exists in substantial part because government officials themselves cannot be trusted with unlimited authority.

The Founders understood something that the kindergarten analogy risks overlooking: The people occupying positions of power are not necessarily wiser, more virtuous, or less susceptible to selfishness than the people they govern. Indeed, public office may provide extraordinary opportunities for those human weaknesses to produce widespread harm. James Madison captured the fundamental problem in Federalist No. 51 when he observed, “If men were angels, no government would be necessary.” His point was not that government should resemble an affectionate classroom, but that governmental power must be restrained because the people exercising it possess the same imperfections as everyone else. The constitutional solution was not to appoint an all-powerful teacher. It was to divide authority, establish checks and balances, and protect individual liberty against abuses of power.

There is a particularly amusing contradiction in the suggestion that society consists of oversized kindergarteners. If everyone is essentially a kindergartner, that presumably includes the politicians proposing to supervise everyone else. It includes members of Congress, governors, federal regulators, judges, cabinet secretaries, and the officials entrusted with managing the national economy. If the population cannot be trusted to exercise adult judgment, why should anyone assume that those holding political office have somehow graduated from the same condition? The argument collapses under its own premise. Either adults possess the capacity for responsible self-government, or there is no obvious reason to grant extraordinary power to a select group of them merely because they won an election.

There is also an important distinction between kindness as a personal virtue and kindness as a substitute for public policy. Encouraging children to share, cooperate, respect others, and resolve disputes peacefully is admirable. Adults should practice those principles whenever circumstances permit. But a government must also make difficult decisions involving criminal conduct, international aggression, public safety, economic scarcity, and competing constitutional rights. Compassion does not eliminate the necessity of enforcing laws. Respect for others does not require surrendering national sovereignty. Cooperation does not justify abandoning individual liberties. Sometimes the most responsible action is to say no, impose consequences, or confront someone who refuses to respect the rights of others.

Talarico's own background makes the comparison especially interesting. He previously taught sixth-grade language arts in San Antonio and has made public education a central element of his political career. He has described his classroom experiences as instrumental in motivating his entry into politics. That experience provides a reasonable explanation for his use of educational imagery, and it would be unfair to conclude from a nine-second excerpt that he literally wants Congress to distribute crayons or replace criminal sentencing with time-outs. The criticism here concerns the implications of taking his metaphor seriously, not a claim that these satirical policies appear in his legislative platform.

Nevertheless, political metaphors matter because they reveal how leaders conceptualize the relationship between citizens and institutions. Describing society as a family suggests parental obligations. Describing government as a business emphasizes efficiency and measurable results. Describing the nation as a military unit emphasizes discipline, hierarchy, and collective objectives. Describing the world as a kindergarten classroom naturally raises questions about supervision, dependence, behavioral management, and the authority of those entrusted with maintaining order. Those implications deserve scrutiny even when the original speaker intended nothing more ambitious than an appeal for kindness.

And this brings us to the most important fact about kindergarten, one that the entire political comparison seems to overlook. Kindergarten is not supposed to be permanent. Its purpose is to help children develop the intellectual, social, and emotional capabilities necessary to progress toward greater independence. Students learn to communicate, solve problems, exercise judgment, manage disagreements, accept consequences, and take increasing responsibility for themselves. They advance to first grade, then through subsequent years of education, and eventually into adulthood. The ultimate objective is not to create lifelong kindergarten students who require perpetual supervision. It is to develop competent individuals capable of functioning without it.

An adult society organized around permanent dependency would reverse that process. Rather than encouraging citizens to think independently, it would encourage them to seek official approval. Rather than teaching individuals to manage risk and accept responsibility, it would invite them to transfer those obligations to government. Rather than treating liberty as an inherent condition accompanied by personal duties, it would increasingly portray freedom as a privilege administered by political authorities. The result would not necessarily be a kinder civilization. It could become a society in which government accumulated greater power while citizens surrendered the responsibilities that make self-government possible.

The irony is that many of the behaviors supposedly associated with kindergarten are already evident in modern politics. Elected officials engage in public tantrums, refuse to cooperate with people they dislike, interrupt one another, assign blame for their own failures, make promises they cannot keep, and sometimes behave as though the entire world revolves around them. Political parties increasingly treat disagreement as a personal offense, while public debate frequently resembles a playground argument in which everyone shouts and nobody listens. Perhaps Talarico has identified a genuine problem after all, although the logical response would be to demand that political leaders demonstrate greater maturity rather than reorganize the entire country around their existing level of behavior.

Imagine a kindergarten teacher watching two children quarrel over the same toy. The teacher intervenes, establishes boundaries, explains the importance of respecting others, and helps the children find a peaceful resolution. That is good teaching. Now imagine applying the same procedure to a dictator ordering the invasion of a neighboring country, a terrorist organization planning a massacre, or a corrupt official deliberately stealing public funds. The superficial similarity disappears almost immediately. The world contains problems that cannot be solved through reassurance, problems that require the application of law, the exercise of legitimate authority, and sometimes the use of force. A leader unwilling to recognize those distinctions is not demonstrating superior compassion. He is demonstrating an inadequate understanding of the responsibilities of leadership.

The same lesson applies to domestic governance. Americans are not obligated to agree with one another, share identical values, endorse the same political candidates, or organize their lives around a government-approved conception of happiness. The Constitution provides a framework within which people holding profoundly different beliefs can coexist while retaining fundamental liberties. That system can be contentious, frustrating, and occasionally unpleasant. It also protects something far more important than universal agreement: the right of individuals to govern their own lives without unnecessary interference from the state.

There is nothing objectionable about wanting adults to treat one another with greater kindness. Most Americans would welcome less hostility, more cooperation, greater honesty, and a stronger sense of personal responsibility. But those objectives are not achieved by confusing adult citizenship with childhood dependence. They are achieved when individuals recognize that freedom comes with obligations, that rights belong to others as well as themselves, and that legitimate authority must always remain answerable to the people it serves.

THE VERDICT

James Talarico's kindergarten remark offers a useful political thought experiment, although perhaps not quite the one he intended. Taken as an appeal for civility, cooperation, and compassion, the sentiment is understandable. Taken literally as a model for governing the world, it becomes an absurdity that exposes the dangers of paternalism, centralized supervision, and the substitution of reassuring language for adult responsibility.

America does not need a government that treats its citizens like children. It needs a government that respects their rights, enforces the law, protects the country, manages public resources responsibly, and recognizes the constitutional limits of its own authority. Citizens do not require politicians to supervise their feelings, distribute participation awards, or promise that nobody will ever experience disappointment. They require institutions that function, laws that are applied fairly, and public officials capable of understanding that holding office does not make them intellectually or morally superior to the people who elected them.

If Washington genuinely adopted kindergarten standards, perhaps the first rule should be that lying is unacceptable, taking what belongs to someone else is wrong, bullying is prohibited, and everyone must clean up the messes they create. Applied consistently, those elementary principles might disqualify a remarkable number of politicians before the first morning recess. Unfortunately, enforcing them would require a level of accountability that Washington has spent decades attempting to avoid.

The Founders did not establish a republic so that future generations could surrender their independence to a permanent classroom administration. They established a constitutional system designed to preserve liberty while restraining the inevitable abuses of human authority. The entire premise rests upon the expectation that citizens are capable of exercising judgment, accepting responsibility, and participating in their own government.

Perhaps there is one kindergarten lesson worth passing along to every politician in Washington, including James Talarico. It is the lesson that every competent kindergarten teacher ultimately hopes to impart to the children entrusted to their care.

The whole purpose of kindergarten is to prepare you to leave it.

America has already graduated.

It does not need to enroll again.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

I doubt the story is true. But a good read. Moral of the story, plan ahead. Prior planning prevents emergencies from becoming communal burdens in numerous aspects of life from retirement to power outages to health.

HOUSTON, Texas — A 41-year-old homeowner sparked a neighborhood dispute after refusing to let nearby residents use his generator for free during a three-day power outage.

The man had purchased the $4,000 generator after a previous storm left his family without electricity for nearly a week.

When another outage struck, several neighbors approached him asking to charge devices, refrigerate groceries and power household appliances.

He agreed to help but requested $100 per household to cover fuel, maintenance and the inconvenience of managing additional connections.

Some neighbors paid, while others accused him of profiting from an emergency.

text:
It’s quiet, too quiet……

This market is suspect, the next dip is the one I’m looking to get into though. Looks like we’re raw dogging into midterms with no deal. Seeing all the diplomatic breakthroughs last week made it seem that the chances were high that we get a deal before the midterms, but nah that’s not happening here and so Midterms is the catalyst here. Republicans aint getting a Hail Mary like I expected but instead will get a nasty defensive grind Patriots type of win. I just look at the Zeitgeist and it just has no edge in anything right now, every crowd sourced answer to any market questions since the Summer has just be wrong. The crowd is not seeing the ball here and that’s why I would define this market regime as just pure inertia. So that’s where I stand when assessing midterms, I just think the crowd/polls are pwrong here and think the pain trade is that they are wrong, as they have been for some time now.  

A lack of a Democratic Sweep should be bullish though and at least turn the toggle back on for markets to be bullish again. Avoiding a blue sweep will offer more than respite, it will change the calculus of many participants in major ways. This is a market living in fear of underperformance heading into year end and so getting clarity on midterms will ground the market and finally make it resolve in one direction, something bulls and bears yearn to see. The market will still need that deal for the throttle though, which I expect. 

My bond proxies finally getting life though so that’s good to see, that will embolden me to buy the dip when it comes, as it just feels like we got one more dip here left. I’ve been bullish but haven’t been buying dips but will do so on the next impulse down if we get one. No one has asymmetric edge in terms of why they are buying or selling, they’re just placing bets, so if you see massive flows in one direction, then the pain trade becomes inertia. This really has been the case since the Summer. Retail aping in on Friday smells like this as the pros won’t come back in until we get clarity on Midterms. Sets us up for a volatile next two days, but it’ll be a great opportunity for the patient and prudent.

Don’t underestimate the risk heading into midterms these next two days and the risk coming out of midterms, as those are two different opportunity sets.

text:
THE SONS OF THE SERPENT TRIBE
OPHIOLATREIA

Original Title Page from FIRST (& Only Original) Edition

D. OPHIOLATREIA
THE following comes from Chapter 1 of Ophiolatreia, anonymously written by Hargrave Jennings:

In Egypt was a serpent named Thermuthis, which was looked upon as very sacred; and the natives are said to have made use of it as a royal tiara, with which they ornamented the statues of Isis. We learn from Diodorus Siculus that the kings of Egypt wore high bonnets, which terminated in a round ball, and the whole was surrounded by figures of asps. The priests, likewise, upon their bonnets had the representation of serpents. The ancients had a notion that when Saturn devoured his own children, his wife Ops deceived him by substituting a large stone in lieu of one of his sons, which stone was called Abadir. But Ops and Opis, represented here as a feminine, was the serpent deity, and Abadir is the same personage under a different denomination. Abadir seems to be a variation of Ob-Adur, and signifies the serpent god Orus. One of these stones, which Saturn was supposed to have swallowed instead of a child, stood, according to Pausanias, at Delphi. It was esteemed very sacred, and used to have libations of wine poured upon it daily; and upon festivals was otherwise honoured. The purport of the above was probably this: it was for a long time a custom to offer children at the altar of Saturn; but in process of time they removed it, and in its room erected a stone pillar, before which they made their vows, and offered sacrifices of another nature. This stone which they thus substituted was called Ab-Adar, from the deity represented by it. The term Ab generally signifies a father, but in this instance it certainly relates to a serpent, which was indifferently styled Ab, Aub, and Ob. Some regard Abadon, or, as it is mentioned in the Book of the Revelation, Abaddon, to have been the name of the same Ophite god, with whose worship the world had been so long infected. He is termed Abaddon, the angel of the bottomless pit - the prince of darkness. In another place he is described as the dragon, that old serpent, which is the devil, and Satan. Hence the learned Heinsius is supposed to be right in the opinion which he has given upon this passage, when he makes Abaddon the same as the serpent Pytho.

It is said that in the ritual of Zoroaster the great expanse of the heavens, and even nature itself, was described under the symbol of a serpent. [Note: Eusebius.] The like was mentioned in the Octateuch of Ostanes; and moreover, in Persia and in other parts of the East they erected temples to the serpent tribe, and held festivals to their honour, esteeming them the supreme of all Gods, and the superintendants of the whole world. The worship began among the people of Chaldea. They built the city Opis upon the Tigris, and were greatly addicted to divination and to the worship of the serpent. From Chaldea the worship passed into Egypt, where the serpent deity was called Canoph, Caneph, and C'neph. It had also the name of Ob, or Oub, and was the same as the Basilicus, or Royal Serpent; the same also as the Thermuthis, and in like manner was made use of by way of ornament to the statues of their Gods. The chief Deity of Egypt is said to have been Vulcan, who was also styled Opas, as we learn from Cicero. He was the same as Osiris, the Sun; and hence was often called Ob-El, or Pytho-Sol; and there were pillars sacred to him, with curious hieroglyphical inscriptions, which had the same name. They were very lofty, and narrow in comparison of their length; hence among the Greeks, who copied from the Egyptians, everything gradually tapering to a point was styled Obelos, and Obeliscus. Ophel (Oph-El) was a name of the same purport, and many sacred mounds, or Tapha, were thus denominated from the serpent Deity, to whom they were sacred.

Sanchoniathon makes mention of a history which he once wrote upon the worship of the serpent. The title of this work, according to Eusebius, was Ethothion, or Ethothia. Another treatise upon the same subject was written by Pherecydes Tyrus, which was probably a copy of the former; for he is said to have composed it from some previous accounts of the Phoenicians. The title of his book was the Theology of Ophion, styled Ophioneus, and his worshippers were called Ophionidae. Thoth and Athoth were certainly titles of the Deity in the Gentile world; and the book of Sanchoniathon might very possibly have been from hence named Ethothion, or more truly, Athothion. But, from the subject upon which it was written, as well as from the treatise of Pherecydes, we have reason to think that Athothion, or Ethothion, was a mistake for Ath-Ophion, a title which more immediately related to that worship of which the writer treated. Ath was a sacred title, as we have shewn, and we imagine that this dissertation did not barely relate to the serpentine Deity, but contained accounts of his votaries, the Ophites, the principal of which were the sons of Chus. The worship of the serpent began among them, and they were from thence denominated Ethiopians, and Aithopians, which the Greeks rendered Aithiopes. They did not receive this name from their complexion, as has sometimes been surmised, for the branch of Phut and the Luhim, were probably of a deeper dye; but they were most likely so called from Ath-Ope, and Ath-Opis, the God which they worshipped. This may be shewn from Pliny. He says that the country Ethiopia (and consequently the people), had the name of Aethiop, from a personage who was a Deity - ob Aethiope Vulcani filio. The Aethiopes brought these rites into Greece, and called the island where they first established them Ellopia, Solis Serpentis insula. It was the same as Euboea, a name of the like purport, in which island was a region named Ethiopium. Euboea is properly Oub-Aia, and signifies, the Serpent Island. The same worship prevailed among the Hyperboreans, as we may judge from the names of the sacred women who used to come annually to Delos; they were priestesses of the Tauric Goddess. Hercules was esteemed the chief God, the same as Chronus, and was said to have produced the Mundane egg. He was represented in the Orphic theology under the mixed symbol of a lion and a serpent, and sometimes of a serpent only.

The Cuthites, under the title of Heliadae, having settled at Rhodes, as they were Hivites, or Ophites, the island was in consequence named Ophiusa. There was likewise a tradition that it had once swarmed with serpents. (Bochart says the island is said to have been named Rhodus from Rhad, a Syriac word for a serpent). The like notion prevailed almost in every place where they settled. They came under the more general titles of Leleges and Pelasgi; but more particularly of Elopians, Europians, Oropians, Asopians, Inopians, Ophionians, and Aethiopes, as appears from the names which they bequeathed; and in most places where they resided there were handed down traditions which alluded to their original title of Ophites. In Phrygia, and upon the Hellespont, whither they sent out colonies very early, was a people styled the Ophiogeneis, or the serpent breed, who were said to retain an affinity and correspondence with serpents; and a notion prevailed that some hero, who had conducted them, was changed from a serpent to a man. In Colchis was a river Ophis, and there was another of the same name in Arcadia. It was so named from a body of people who settled upon its banks, and were said to have been conducted by a serpent.

It is said these reptiles are seldom found in islands, but that Tenos, one of the Cyclades, was supposed to have once swarmed with them. [Note: Aristoph.]

Thucydides mentions a people of Aetotia, called Ophionians; and the temple of Apollo at Petara, in Lycia, seems to have had its first institution from a priestess of the same name. The island of Cyprus was called Ophiusa, and Ophiodes, from the serpents with which it was supposed to have abounded. Of what species they were is nowhere mentioned, excepting only that about Paphos there was said to have been a kind of serpent with two legs. By this is meant the Ophite race, who came from Egypt, and from Syria, and got footing in this island. They settled also in Crete, where they increased greatly in numbers; so that Minos was said by an unseemly allegory, opheis ouresai, serpentes, minxisse. The island Seriphus was one vast rock, by the Romans called saxum seriphium, and made use of as a large kind of prison for banished persons. It is represented as having once abounded with serpents, and it is styled by Virgil, serpentifera, as the passage is corrected by Scaliger.

It is said by the Greeks that Medusa's head was brought by Perseus; by this is meant the serpent Deity, whose worship was here introduced by people called Peresians. Medusa's head denoted divine wisdom, and the island was sacred to the serpent, as is apparent from its name. The Athenians were esteemed Serpentiginae, and they had a tradition that the chief guardian of their Acropolis was a serpent.

It is reported of the goddess Ceres that she placed a dragon for a guardian to her temple at Eleusis, and appointed another to attend upon Erectheus. Aegeus of Athens, according to Androtion, was of the serpent breed, and the first king of the country is said to have been a dragon. Others make Cecrops the first who reigned. He is said to have been of a two-fold nature, being formed with the body of a man blended with that of a serpent.

Diodorus says that this was a circumstance deemed by the Athenians inexplicable; yet he labours to explain it by representing Cecrops as half a man and half a brute, because he had been of two different communities. Eustathius likewise tries to solve it nearly upon the same principles, and with the like success. Some have said of Cecrops that he underwent a metamorphosis, being changed from a serpent to a man. By this was meant, according to Eustathius, that Cecrops by coming into Hellas divested himself of all the rudeness and barbarity of his country, and became more civilised and human. This is declared by some to be too high a compliment to be paid to Greece in its infant state, and detracts greatly from the character of the Egyptians. The learned Marsham therefore animadverts with great justice, "it is more probable that he introduced into Greece the urbanity of his own country, than that he was beholden to Greece for anything from thence." In respect to the mixed character of this personage, we may easily account for it. Cecrops was certainly a title of the Deity, who was worshipped under this emblem. Something of the like nature was mentioned of Triptolemus and Erichtonius, and the like has been said of Hercules. The natives of Thebes in Boeotia, like the Athenians, esteemed themselves of the serpent race. The Lacedaemonians likewise referred themselves to the same original. Their city is said of old to have swarmed with serpents. The same is said of the city Amyelae in Italy, which was of Spartan origin. They came hither in such abundance that it was abandoned by the inhabitants. Argos was infested in the same manner till Apis came from Egypt and settled in that city. He was a prophet, the reputed son of Apollo, anda person of great skill and sagacity, and to him they attributed the blessing of having their country freed from this evil. Thus the Argives gave the credit to this imaginary personage of clearing their land of this grievance, but the brood came from the very quarter from whence Apis was supposed to have arrived. They were certainly Hivites from Egypt, and the same story is told of that country. It is represented as having been of old over-run with serpents, and almost depopulated through their numbers. Diodorus Siculus seems to understand this literally, but a region that was annually overflowed, and that too for so long a season, could not well be liable to such a calamity. They were serpents of another nature with which it was thus infested, and the history relates to the Cuthites, the original Ophitae, who for a long time possessed that country. They passed from Egypt to Syria, and to the Euphrates, and mention is made of a particular breed of serpents upon that river, which were harmless to the natives but fatal to anybody else. This can hardly be taken literally; for whatever may be the wisdom of the serpent it cannot be sufficient to make these distinctions. These serpents were of the same nature as the birds of Diomedes, and the dogs in the temple of Vulcan; and the histories relate to Ophite priests, who used to spare their own people and sacrifice strangers, a custom which prevailed at one time in most parts of the world. The Cuthite priests are said to have been very learned; and, as they were Ophites, whoever had the advantage of their information was said to have been instructed by serpents.

As the worship of the serpent was of old so prevalent, many places, as well as people, from thence received their names. Those who settled in Campania were called Opici, which some would have changed to Ophici, because they were denominated from serpents. They are in reality both names of the same purport, and denote the origin of the people.

We meet with places called Opis, Ophis, Ophitaea, Ophionia, Ophioessa, Ophiodes, and Ophiusa. This last was an ancient name by which, according to Stephanus, the islands Rhodes, Cynthus, Besbicus, Tenos, and the whole continent of Africa, were distinguished. There were also cities so-called. Add to these places denominated Oboth, Obona, and reversed, Onoba, from Ob, which was of the same purport.

Clemens Alexandrinus says that the term Eva signified a serpent if pronounced with a proper aspirate, and Epiphanius says the same thing. We find that there were places of this name. There was a city Eva in Arcadia, and another in Macedonia. There was also a mountain Eva, or Evan, taken notice of by Pausanias, between which and Ithome lay the city Messene. He mentions also an Eva in Argolis, and speaks of it as a large town. Another name for a serpent, which we have not yet noticed, was Patan, or Pitan. Many places in different parts were denominated from this term. Among others was a city in Laconia, and another in Mysia, which Stephanus styles a city of Aeolia. They were undoubtedly so named from the worship of the serpent, Pitan, and had probably Dracontia, which were figures and devices relative to the religion which prevailed. Ovid mentions the latter city, and has some allusions to its ancient history when he describes Medea as flying through the air from Athea to Colchis. The city was situate upon the ruin Eva, or Evan, which the Greeks rendered Evenus. According to Strabo it is compounded of Eve-Ain, the fountain or river of Eva the serpent.

It is remarkable that the Opici, who are said to have been named from serpents, had also the name of Pitanatae; at least, one part of that family was so-called. Pitanatae is a term of the same purport as Opici, and relates to the votaries of Pitan, the serpent Deity, which was adored by that people. Menelaus was of old called Pitanates, as we learn from Hesychius, and the reason of it may be known from his being a Spartan, by which he was intimated one of the Serpentigenae, or Ophites. Hence he was represented with a serpent for a device upon his shield. It is said that a brigade, or portion of infantry, was among some of the Greeks named Pitanates, and the soldiers in consequence of it must have been termed Pitanatae, undoubtedly, because they had the Pitan, or serpent, for their standard. Analogous to this, among other nations there were soldiers called Draconarii. In most countries the military standard was an emblem of the Deity there worshipped.

What has already been said has thrown some light upon the history of this primitive idolatry, and we have shewn that wherever any of these Ophite colonies settled, they left behind from their rites and institutions, as well as from the names which they bequeathed to places, ample memorials, by which they may be clearly traced out.
- Ophiolatreia, pp. 3-9.

E. COMMENTS
There are many themes presented above, which we have come across previously. We think it fair to say that the Serpent Breed, or Serpent Tribe, is none other than the human offspring and/or incarnations of the Anunnaki. Let us assume for a moment that what we have just quoted above is a work of True History. That is, if True ESOTERIC History. Even today, we know precious little about what actually happened in the past, especially in the past of, say, 3000 years ago. We know that several kingdoms existed, such as Babylonia, Egypt, India, Phoenicia, and other places existed. But - how did the Esoteric Cultus survive, from the days of Sumer, to today? And what is to account for the conscious memory of Humankind suddenly coming to life in the 7th - 6th centuries B.C.E.?

This lengthy extract is basically a short account of what General Forlong devotes 230 pages in volume one of his excellent survey, Rivers of Life: to Tree and Serpent Worship.

Some of these things can be plotted on the map, and on the historical timeline. Perhaps a great deal is fabulous, or at the least is "myth" - history turned into fiction for certain people of today to regard as bunk. Well, we do not regard any of it as bunk.

One of the main strands of the story is given in this extract - that of the Aethiopes. We have come across traces of this story in several different places. In fact, we can see a story that goes back to the destruction of Sumer, to the migrations that followed that destruction, and to a survival of various cults in the region to the North and West of India.

Eventually, some of these Priests are exiled and come across, by way of the Island of the Dioscuri - Socotra. Some travel up the Incense Route, and end up in the Nabatean regions and in Palestine. Some go across to Ethiopia, and from there to Egypt. By the time the Priesthood of the Solis Serpentis reaches Egypt, we are getting close to the time of Akhnaten. After the demise of Akhnaten, and his religion, some of our Priests migrate north, and across the Mediterranean, to Euboea. We can take it from there in the next extract, below, from the Dionysian Artificers, by Da Costa.

It is necessary to go into the past, beyond the birth of the Gnosis, to the Near-Eastern Serpent Cults, and to the Mystery Traditions, and perhaps to the oldest cults we can find traces of, in order to view the Current as a continuous whole, a continuity as complete as the Ouroboros itself.

F. ORIGINS OF SERPENT GODS
Zecharia Sitchin points out that EnKi was given Africa, while EnLil had Mesopotamia, Inanna the Indus Valley, and NinHarsag the Sinai Peninsula. Notice that the Ethiopians, according to Jennings, were called the sons of Vulcan. This is the same appellation given to Adapa and Enmeduranki. Vulcan is none other than Ptah, who is none other than EnKi, according to popular syncretization. Interestingly, Im-Hetep, or Imouthis, is given as Ptah's son, in the Memphite Triad. Imouthis is also known as Asklepios, who is also known as Agathodaimon. Also, I-M-Hetep is known as the first important builder in Egyptian history, as well as being a physician. Interesting.

Also, the Cuthites may be like the Cuthans, mentioned above, but they are also confused with the Cushites, or sons of Cush. The Cushites came from the Land of Cush, which is known to be Nubia and Ethiopia.

It is stated that these Cuthites migrated from Egypt, to Syria, to the Euphrates. Also it is said that the Aith-Opes or Ethiopians migrated to Greece, and brought the rites of Serpent worship with them. Also, in connection with this it is said that Erectheus is the individual responsible for bringing the rites of Eleusis to Greece, to Athens. Now, could these Cuthites be connected with the Babylonian Priests we have spoken of, i.e., the Nergals of Cutha? Perhaps. We know that about 43 miles north of Baghdad on the west bank of the Tigris river is the location of the ancient city of Opis, where at least two crucial events took place. First, this is where the Persians, under the command of Cyrus, overthrew Babylon and claimed the whole area as a satrapy. Second, this is where Alexander the Great was said to have invited dignitaries from all over his empire for the purpose of feasting and so that he could consolidate them all together and proclaim his New World Order.

As can be seen, these legendary stories may not be so legendary after all. Competent scholars are confirming the legends bit by bit, even if they would regard these legends as little more than fictions. The work we just quoted above may not have been written by an expert academician of high repute, whatever that is supposed to indicate, but Brother Jennings was an Adept of high repute, and drew from a wide variety of classical sources, some of which not everybody has access to, especially today. The fact that a High Initiate wrote the above really should be no bar to its believability, or to its credibility.

Interested parties (that is, those with agendas) including some Freemasons in the mix, as well as their opponents continue to prefer denial of all stories of the past which conflict with their preconceived notions. It is safer to assume that the Craft is somehow attached to the craft guilds of the 17th century and became Freemasonry in 1717. It is safer to relegate history to something else, far removed from our own roots.

For those of us in whom the Historical Tradition is The Path, and that by which we HAVE Attained much, this is all rather ludicrous. That which is still condemned today as heresy, perhaps should be condemned as heresy, or as false, in order to keep out the riff raff. Yet, our ancestors practiced the same way as we do now, and when we are condemned as heretics, we can point to our traditional lineage. And - we no longer have to hear people remark that this is all new heresy, either, for it has a very ancient background.

Similarly, it is much safer for a fundamentalist to believe that the Bible as it exists today was dictated as such by the finger of God, even though the King James version is not as accurate a translation of the ancient texts as one can get, and even though Shakespearian English did not exist 2,000 and more years ago. And, the fundamentalist reader will believe our accounts when we speak of things which they consider to be evil, but are grossly ignorant as to their true purport. Then we get rocks thrown at us, when we attempt to show, that what has been considered evil throughout the centuries, is actually not evil at all, and in fact is the legitimate truth, and that which has been considered good is the real heresy, intended for the slaves to follow to their hearts' content.

So, when we speak of Pagan connections, Gnostic survivals and the like, we (and those that we are really writing this material for) see Triumph, Praise, Truth. But when our adversaries see these things in print, they are convinced we are antichrists and that we are perverted, doomed, and damned.

Yet, they have had the blinds of ignorance (with the help of "saint" Paul and others of his ilk) controlling all that they see, hear, or think, like the Control Voice on The Outer Limits. And their ministers, or shepherds, control the vertical as well! But - we can see in all we have researched, and all that we present here, a pattern that goes way back as far as we can reckon, and spreads from Morocco, Spain and the British Isles east as far as China, Korea, and Japan. When we add the "New World" to the mix, we can add North , Central, and South America as well, and while we're at it, the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans, too.

G - A MESSAGE FROM "COUNT WELLDONE"
Greetings, Fellow Prophets!

In Antediluvian times, or prior to the year 10,973 B. C. E., this sect existed. It still exists to this very day. No, we are not speaking the same bilge about Atlanteans and Lemurians, and adding all the famous names of the past to our list to give us a built-in pedigree. We are not going to take the holier-than-thou attitude like the people that are convinced that they get messages from my alter Saint-Germain. No, because we must pity their ignorance and child-like innocence we shall leave their condemnation to the Law of Karma for having led millions astray with the swill they preach, publish and get rich from.

Anyone notice any similarities between Oswald’s strange choice of Albert Schweitzer College in Switzerland, which each Swiss had never fucking heard of —though that’s perhaps an easy league — and  the CIA Medical college in Grenada and the very medically savvy Jonestown People’s Temple compound in Guyana?“In mid-March of 1959, Oswald somehow picked up an application to attend Albert Schweitzer College (ASC). He applied for the spring term of 1960. As some commentators have noted, Schweitzer was a college in name only, since it offered no degrees. 94 It began as a lecture series by one Hans Casparis. Casparis then expanded the offerings with help from various individuals from the USA and also the Unitarian Church, which also played a part in its administration. In 1953, because of this financial outreach, Casparis purchased the former Hotel Krone in Churwalden, a five story, thirty-room building and announced the opening of the “college.” 95 The location of ASC was odd. It was high in the Swiss Alps, fifteen miles from the industrial town of Chur. There was only one main road winding through the town and into the Alps. The school accommodated only thirty students, yet Schweitzer listed sixty-eight individuals as representatives and references of the college. 96 There was no bus or railway service to the village and no library, hospital, fire department, or police station. The college officially opened to students in the fall of 1955. Yet in the entering class of thirty, none were from Switzerland. This may have been deliberate, in order not to have to register or be accredited with the Swiss government. As we shall see the college was virtually unknown to Swiss authorities. In fact, when the FBI tried to find the place, it transferred the request to agents in Paris. Even they had never heard of it, so they contacted the Swiss police. It took the Swiss police two months to find Albert Schweitzer. If the idea was to keep a low profile, it was achieved. 97 Since there were so few students attending, the school had to get by on donations from benefactors. The American Committee of Friends of Albert Schweitzer College was incorporated in New York but had its offices in Boston. The head of the American Admissions Committee was Unitarian Church Minister Dr. Robert Schact of Providence. It was Schact who cleared Oswald’s application and sent it to Switzerland for final disposition. 98 When Marguerite Oswald wrote her son a series of letters in Russia in late 1959, she enclosed money orders. She got no reply except a returned letter. She was worried he might be lost. She alerted the FBI to the fact that she had gotten a letter from Casparis saying that Lee was expected there in April of 1960. He had been accepted and his application fee had been deposited. She was visited by FBI agent John Fain in April of 1960. Marguerite told Fain about the returned letters and how Lee was apparently lost in Russia. Now, J. Edgar Hoover began to search for Casparis and his college. This search occasioned the famous June 3, 1960, memo by Hoover saying that there is a possibility that an imposter is using Oswald’s birth certificate. It turned out that Oswald never went to Schweitzer. But the question that remains, which the Commission never answered is: How did Oswald ever hear of this obscure institution halfway around the world while he was in Santa Ana? Because, as has been shown, the college did not advertise in the Christian Register from 1948–59.99 Was it brought to Oswald’s attention by Kerry Thornley? Thornley testified that he had been going to the First Unitarian Church in Los Angeles around the time he met Oswald. 100 Author George Michael Evica also explored the career of Hans Casparis, who wrote that he had graduated from three universities and lectured at the University of Zurich. THE RECORD, DECLARED

IN THE ROYAL HOUSE OF GOOSE, November 1, 2026.
The Register Current of the Grievances of a Citizen of the United States of America

Every petition, inquiry, indictment, condemnation and damnation raised from this account, collected in one place, in the order raised, each beside its link. Each was declared in its own post, on its own sources, quoted from the documents themselves. Read them whole.

"A decent respect to the opinions of mankind requires that they should declare the causes." They have been declared, one by one. Here they are, together.

"To prove this, let Facts be submitted to a candid world."

WHERE IT BEGAN

WE THE PEOPLE · https://t.co/iPLyJ0zPEH
Against all 535 seated members of the 119th Congress
The first grievance, the one that opened the door. Six FY2026 bills, the defense authorization among them, charged section by section: reporting, notification, reprogramming and force-posture mandates that encroach on the President's powers under Article II. It asks the governors and attorneys general to seek Supreme Court review, and every State to investigate the financial backers of its delegation for foreign influence. Closed on Washington's Farewell Address.
https://t.co/JiqZZtMvOW

THE PETITION, THE INQUIRY AND THE INDICTMENTS

THE PETITION · to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Pope
A plea for the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness," raised in the Church's own law: in Latin, by a lay member of the faithful, under canon 212. To the Dicastery: a doctrinal Note declaring priests and prelates bound to put innocent human life before any temporal political end, and a declaration that their public, obstinate denial of the teaching John Paul II confirmed in Evangelium vitae 57 falls under penal law. To the Pope: a common effort with the Eastern Churches, in communion or not, to protect innocent children born and unborn; and a worldwide review of Church property accounts, so that no political influence bends the refuge the Church offers the needy.
https://t.co/UNnZwyrpQi

THE BANNER · A Citizen's Indictment and Condemnation
Against the ICC, the ICJ, the UN, the WTO, the EU, and the committees of Basel and Paris
The Constitution, the Uniform Code of Military Justice and the Declaration raised against every body that would bind Americans to law they never ratified. Six counts, each set against the clause it offends. Our rights are not granted by government; they are fenced off from it. Then the record of every time since 1919 the question was put and the Constitution answered it, even when our own Presidents were the ones asking.
https://t.co/NgTe8NVuBZ

BEFORE THE DAIS · An Inquiry
To the eight living Secretaries of State
Not a charge against any of them: a charge against what the office has been allowed to become. The standard Hamilton, Jay, Jefferson and the Foreign Service Act set for it, against what the government's own auditors found: fitness written as "should," training by accretion, posts left empty, authority on paper, and a revolving-door guard that lapses in 2027. Seven questions to all of them, and one to each on their own record. A paragraph each is enough.
https://t.co/pltubkVVeJ

IN CONGRESS ASSEMBLED · A Citizen's Indictment of the First Branch
Against the Senate and the House, under every majority that has held them
Nine counts: the purse let fall; war made without a declaration since 1942; the legislative power parcelled out to the agencies, the Federal Reserve and Basel; the legislative veto; the courts left unbuilt; a House grown to one member for every 761,169; judges in their own cause; the faction; and the enforcement clauses left asleep. The Declaration charged a King with power seized. These are charges of power abandoned: "He has abdicated Government here." Answer by the yeas and nays.
https://t.co/jAVsOSRHPl

ONE SUPREME COURT · A Citizen's Indictment of the Third Branch
Against the Court, and the Chief Justice who alone designates its secret benches
Ten counts on three duties. To check the branches: forty years of deference, a surveillance bench the watched cannot reach, the jury bargained away, courts it did not make, rights signed away in fine print. To judge between the States: sovereign States turned away from the only court they have. To guard the sovereignty: foreign custom let in by a second door, Missouri v. Holland, the Insular Cases, and the citizenship it would not decide. Answer by judgment, in a case.
https://t.co/vywTIPdChv

THE ROUNDS

ROUND I · THE EU · The Exits Already Written
Twenty U.S.–EU agreements the Executive may end on written notice, by their own terms, read out of the State Department's own Treaties in Force: passenger-name records, terrorist-finance tracking, Europol, Galileo–GPS and the air transport agreement among them. A nominal list of what can be done alone; the weighing is State's and Treasury's. The first of a round for every State, non-state actor and non-U.S. body that gets uppity with us.
https://t.co/smLQ4MK6jL

ROUND II · THE EBRD · The Door Already Written
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, charged in its own words; the way out, in its own charter. America paid for a bank to build open markets and private enterprise, and now stands behind one that pledges half its financing to green purposes, aligns every new investment to a treaty America left, takes its nature goals from a convention America never ratified, and names Brussels its largest green donor. ROUND III · FRANCE · From the Present Time and Forever
A damnation of the French Republic, on France's own signature to the treaties of 1778. Fourteen counts, 1775 to 2019: help that came deniable and invoiced, an alliance that was a leash, our independence chained to a Spanish rock, our election worked from outside, our ships seized against its written promise, a throne raised on our border while the Union bled, a door opened to Japan, NATO shown the door. Convicted once already, by Act of Congress in 1798. On the French state, not the French people. Beneath it: what the Executive can end alone, and the dead paper still on the books.

A damnation of the Bank for International Settlements and the committees under its roof: immunity "in time of peace and in time of war," and not one duty owed in return. The mass dissemination machine, charged in one line: censorship, plus mass bullshit distribution. A condemnation of Canada, judged by its own Boundary Waters Treaty: navigation "forever … free and open." Twenty-five counts, 1777 to 2026: the road south for an invading army, raiders sheltered while the Union bled, fishermen seized, milk and quotas rigged, a law against bargaining with us, bourbon pulled from the shelves while Beijing's cars came in. ROUND VII · THE CROWN · Unfeeling Brethren
A damnation of the United Kingdom, in the words Congress struck. In June 1776 Jefferson's draught turned on "our British brethren," and Congress cut its harshest lines lest they give offence. They are restored here: forts kept after the peace, envoys sent home for meddling, American opinion worked in secret, the bank we resolved to kill kept alive, the regimes' money run through our dollar, the enemy's oil insured, burdens handed to us and the ledger kept. A war debt unpaid since the 1930s, its bill run back at Britain's own rules. On the British state, and on the people who returned it to power. Britain only comes second because France exists. Beneath it: 141 exits, clause by clause.
https://t.co/B254o2kMkw

ROUND VIII · AUSTRALIA · The Gateway
Three tiers. A damnation of the government of Australia, judged by ANZUS against the memorandum that made Hobart Beijing's "gateway" to the ice: Darwin's port leased beside our Marines to a Chinese-owned company, a Commissioner who led Brussels and London on speech and tried to set what the whole world may see, Brussels' rules copied in. A condemnation of its failures: goods made by forced labour let in, a Chinese fleet firing live in the Tasman answered with a complaint about the notice, the Pacific lost to Beijing on its watch. And a hand extended to the Australian people, rough, real and as sick of their government's shit as we are of ours: go bilateral, peel off Beijing, lock down Oceania with us. Beneath it: 71 exits open now, clause by clause, 39 of them the Executive's alone.
https://t.co/X4dPDZNnPM

ROUND IX · NATO AND THE UNION · Such Subsidiary Bodies
A damnation of NATO as it stands in 2026, by its own fourteen articles, and of the European Union, for the abuse of American good faith, trust and sacrifice. An alliance that amended itself by communique, made war on a state that attacked no member while our House split 213 to 213, carried our forces past its own map, set middlemen between our forces and our purposes, let us carry about 62 percent of allied defence spending, and gave foreign courts the first claim on our soldiers. A Union that overruled its own peoples and planted its system in our hemisphere. Not against the nations of Europe, save France and England, damned already. To the twenty-seven, line by line: the clause each gave away, and the two doors, Articles 48 and 50. The terms stay within the lock Congress set, and not a piece beyond it.
https://t.co/OOPEwpRluu

ROUND X · THE UN AND DAVOS · Such Other Functions
A damnation of the United Nations, laid by its own Charter, and of the World Economic Forum beside it. A Human Rights Council that seats governments the UN's own investigators accused; a 2019 partnership between the Secretary-General and a Swiss foundation that no organ voted on; American money asked to "accelerate" a recommendation that binds no one; a Charter that opens "WE THE PEOPLES" and has come to treat them as human resources. The Forum: the heads of the European Central Bank, the IMF, the World Bank and the WTO, and BlackRock's chairman, seated as trustees of one Swiss foundation, and a stage where a sitting prime minister proposed ending anonymity on the platforms Americans speak on. Not against the Charter. Not against the nations under it.
https://t.co/iB27hON7lF

ROUND XI · THE AMERICAS · The American Shield
The hemisphere read by its own papers: every agreement in the State Department's Treaties in Force that ties us into it, and every instrument through which Europe reaches in. 760 screened, 576 read whole. The rule of 1823, given treaty form at Havana in 1940, still in force, and built without a door. NATO's line at the Tropic of Cancer, and the Union's own territory south of it, inside Rio's zone. A 1972 extradition treaty still reaching seven British territories, filed under Kiribati and Tuvalu; the Netherlands' own Minister of Finance as our tax partner for three Caribbean islands; a Commission overseer who may "block any or all searches" in a Treasury program. Beneath it: 255 exits the President holds by notice, and 107 Senate-ratified treaties, by citation.
https://t.co/YOcsF8VHbH

ROUND XII · ISRAEL · An Ally in Name
A damnation of the State of Israel, held to its own word: a constitution promised by 1 October 1948 and never written, and a Government its own courts convicted, a secret ballot photographed, an Attorney General subordinated, a High Court ruling refused. Eleven counts: an American ally bombed in its capital; a President forced to write PROHIBITED; peacekeepers under its guns; a NATO ally brought a step from confrontation; ministers who mock us and invite our citizens to leave; paid campaigns aimed at our churches, on the Justice Department's own files; spyware turned on embassy workers; a spy in our Navy; the Liberty. On the Israeli state, not the Israeli people, and not on American Jews, who are Americans. Beneath it: 74 agreements read for their exits, the dead paper still on the books, and the paper we cannot read.

TO THOSE WHO DO HOLD THE POWER
Every one but the petition is a grievance, raised in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances," and laid before the offices that hold the power I do not. I hold no office, and I set no terms. Terms with a foreign power are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry. The purse is the Congress's, consent to treaties is the Senate's, and judgment is the courts'. To each I defer. What touches national security is deferred, without contest, to those who hold it. Where a post sets terms, they are what I would do had I the power, not a demand of those who hold it. The remedies are lawful, and they are the People's: the ballot, Article V, and the petition.

The petition is the Holy See's to answer, and to it I defer: to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Holy Father, that he may act true to the faith he guards and for the good of all mankind. Peter was charged three times to feed the flock, and the lambs first.

We the People

IN CONGRESS, JULY 4, 1776

THE UNANIMOUS DECLARATION OF THE THIRTEEN UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,

WHEN IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS, IT BECOMES NECESSARY FOR ONE PEOPLE TO DISSOLVE THE POLITICAL BANDS WHICH HAVE CONNECTED THEM WITH ANOTHER, AND TO ASSUME AMONG THE POWERS OF THE EARTH, THE SEPARATE AND EQUAL STATION TO WHICH THE LAWS OF NATURE AND OF NATURE'S GOD ENTITLE THEM, A DECENT RESPECT TO THE OPINIONS OF MANKIND REQUIRES THAT THEY SHOULD DECLARE THE CAUSES WHICH IMPEL THEM TO THE SEPARATION.

WE HOLD THESE TRUTHS TO BE SELF-EVIDENT, THAT ALL MEN ARE CREATED EQUAL, THAT THEY ARE ENDOWED BY THEIR CREATOR WITH CERTAIN UNALIENABLE RIGHTS, THAT AMONG THESE ARE LIFE, LIBERTY AND THE PURSUIT OF HAPPINESS.--THAT TO SECURE THESE RIGHTS, GOVERNMENTS ARE INSTITUTED AMONG MEN, DERIVING THEIR JUST POWERS FROM THE CONSENT OF THE GOVERNED, --THAT WHENEVER ANY FORM OF GOVERNMENT BECOMES DESTRUCTIVE OF THESE ENDS, IT IS THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO ALTER OR TO ABOLISH IT, AND TO INSTITUTE NEW GOVERNMENT, LAYING ITS FOUNDATION ON SUCH PRINCIPLES AND ORGANIZING ITS POWERS IN SUCH FORM, AS TO THEM SHALL SEEM MOST LIKELY TO EFFECT THEIR SAFETY AND HAPPINESS. PRUDENCE, INDEED, WILL DICTATE THAT GOVERNMENTS LONG ESTABLISHED SHOULD NOT BE CHANGED FOR LIGHT AND TRANSIENT CAUSES; AND ACCORDINGLY ALL EXPERIENCE HATH SHEWN, THAT MANKIND ARE MORE DISPOSED TO SUFFER, WHILE EVILS ARE SUFFERABLE, THAN TO RIGHT THEMSELVES BY ABOLISHING THE FORMS TO WHICH THEY ARE ACCUSTOMED. BUT WHEN A LONG TRAIN OF ABUSES AND USURPATIONS, PURSUING INVARIABLY THE SAME OBJECT EVINCES A DESIGN TO REDUCE THEM UNDER ABSOLUTE DESPOTISM, IT IS THEIR RIGHT, IT IS THEIR DUTY, TO THROW OFF SUCH GOVERNMENT, AND TO PROVIDE NEW GUARDS FOR THEIR FUTURE SECURITY.--SUCH HAS BEEN THE PATIENT SUFFERANCE OF THESE COLONIES; AND SUCH IS NOW THE NECESSITY WHICH CONSTRAINS THEM TO ALTER THEIR FORMER SYSTEMS OF GOVERNMENT. THE HISTORY OF THE PRESENT KING OF GREAT BRITAIN IS A HISTORY OF REPEATED INJURIES AND USURPATIONS, ALL HAVING IN DIRECT OBJECT THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ABSOLUTE TYRANNY OVER THESE STATES. TO PROVE THIS, LET FACTS BE SUBMITTED TO A CANDID WORLD.

HE HAS REFUSED HIS ASSENT TO LAWS, THE MOST WHOLESOME AND NECESSARY FOR THE PUBLIC GOOD.

HE HAS FORBIDDEN HIS GOVERNORS TO PASS LAWS OF IMMEDIATE AND PRESSING IMPORTANCE, UNLESS SUSPENDED IN THEIR OPERATION TILL HIS ASSENT SHOULD BE OBTAINED; AND WHEN SO SUSPENDED, HE HAS UTTERLY NEGLECTED TO ATTEND TO THEM.

HE HAS REFUSED TO PASS OTHER LAWS FOR THE ACCOMMODATION OF LARGE DISTRICTS OF PEOPLE, UNLESS THOSE PEOPLE WOULD RELINQUISH THE RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURE, A RIGHT INESTIMABLE TO THEM AND FORMIDABLE TO TYRANTS ONLY.

HE HAS CALLED TOGETHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES AT PLACES UNUSUAL, UNCOMFORTABLE, AND DISTANT FROM THE DEPOSITORY OF THEIR PUBLIC RECORDS, FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF FATIGUING THEM INTO COMPLIANCE WITH HIS MEASURES.

HE HAS DISSOLVED REPRESENTATIVE HOUSES REPEATEDLY, FOR OPPOSING WITH MANLY FIRMNESS HIS INVASIONS ON THE RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE.

HE HAS REFUSED FOR A LONG TIME, AFTER SUCH DISSOLUTIONS, TO CAUSE OTHERS TO BE ELECTED; WHEREBY THE LEGISLATIVE POWERS, INCAPABLE OF ANNIHILATION, HAVE RETURNED TO THE PEOPLE AT LARGE FOR THEIR EXERCISE; THE STATE REMAINING IN THE MEAN TIME EXPOSED TO ALL THE DANGERS OF INVASION FROM WITHOUT, AND CONVULSIONS WITHIN.

HE HAS ENDEAVOURED TO PREVENT THE POPULATION OF THESE STATES; FOR THAT PURPOSE OBSTRUCTING THE LAWS FOR NATURALIZATION OF FOREIGNERS; REFUSING TO PASS OTHERS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR MIGRATIONS HITHER, AND RAISING THE CONDITIONS OF NEW APPROPRIATIONS OF LANDS.

HE HAS OBSTRUCTED THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, BY REFUSING HIS ASSENT TO LAWS FOR ESTABLISHING JUDICIARY POWERS.

HE HAS MADE JUDGES DEPENDENT ON HIS WILL ALONE, FOR THE TENURE OF THEIR OFFICES, AND THE AMOUNT AND PAYMENT OF THEIR SALARIES.

HE HAS ERECTED A MULTITUDE OF NEW OFFICES, AND SENT HITHER SWARMS OF OFFICERS TO HARRASS OUR PEOPLE, AND EAT OUT THEIR SUBSTANCE.

HE HAS KEPT AMONG US, IN TIMES OF PEACE, STANDING ARMIES WITHOUT THE CONSENT OF OUR LEGISLATURES.

HE HAS AFFECTED TO RENDER THE MILITARY INDEPENDENT OF AND SUPERIOR TO THE CIVIL POWER.

HE HAS COMBINED WITH OTHERS TO SUBJECT US TO A JURISDICTION FOREIGN TO OUR CONSTITUTION, AND UNACKNOWLEDGED BY OUR LAWS; GIVING HIS ASSENT TO THEIR ACTS OF PRETENDED LEGISLATION:

FOR QUARTERING LARGE BODIES OF ARMED TROOPS AMONG US:

FOR PROTECTING THEM, BY A MOCK TRIAL, FROM PUNISHMENT FOR ANY MURDERS WHICH THEY SHOULD COMMIT ON THE INHABITANTS OF THESE STATES:

FOR CUTTING OFF OUR TRADE WITH ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD:

FOR IMPOSING TAXES ON US WITHOUT OUR CONSENT:

FOR DEPRIVING US IN MANY CASES, OF THE BENEFITS OF TRIAL BY JURY:

FOR TRANSPORTING US BEYOND SEAS TO BE TRIED FOR PRETENDED OFFENCES:

FOR ABOLISHING THE FREE SYSTEM OF ENGLISH LAWS IN A NEIGHBOURING PROVINCE, ESTABLISHING THEREIN AN ARBITRARY GOVERNMENT, AND ENLARGING ITS BOUNDARIES SO AS TO RENDER IT AT ONCE AN EXAMPLE AND FIT INSTRUMENT FOR INTRODUCING THE SAME ABSOLUTE RULE INTO THESE COLONIES:

FOR TAKING AWAY OUR CHARTERS, ABOLISHING OUR MOST VALUABLE LAWS, AND ALTERING FUNDAMENTALLY THE FORMS OF OUR GOVERNMENTS:

FOR SUSPENDING OUR OWN LEGISLATURES, AND DECLARING THEMSELVES INVESTED WITH POWER TO LEGISLATE FOR US IN ALL CASES WHATSOEVER.

HE HAS ABDICATED GOVERNMENT HERE, BY DECLARING US OUT OF HIS PROTECTION AND WAGING WAR AGAINST US.

HE HAS PLUNDERED OUR SEAS, RAVAGED OUR COASTS, BURNT OUR TOWNS, AND DESTROYED THE LIVES OF OUR PEOPLE.

HE IS AT THIS TIME TRANSPORTING LARGE ARMIES OF FOREIGN MERCENARIES TO COMPLEAT THE WORKS OF DEATH, DESOLATION AND TYRANNY, ALREADY BEGUN WITH CIRCUMSTANCES OF CRUELTY & PERFIDY SCARCELY PARALLELED IN THE MOST BARBAROUS AGES, AND TOTALLY UNWORTHY THE HEAD OF A CIVILIZED NATION.

HE HAS CONSTRAINED OUR FELLOW CITIZENS TAKEN CAPTIVE ON THE HIGH SEAS TO BEAR ARMS AGAINST THEIR COUNTRY, TO BECOME THE EXECUTIONERS OF THEIR FRIENDS AND BRETHREN, OR TO FALL THEMSELVES BY THEIR HANDS.

HE HAS EXCITED DOMESTIC INSURRECTIONS AMONGST US, AND HAS ENDEAVOURED TO BRING ON THE INHABITANTS OF OUR FRONTIERS, THE MERCILESS INDIAN SAVAGES, WHOSE KNOWN RULE OF WARFARE, IS AN UNDISTINGUISHED DESTRUCTION OF ALL AGES, SEXES AND CONDITIONS.

IN EVERY STAGE OF THESE OPPRESSIONS WE HAVE PETITIONED FOR REDRESS IN THE MOST HUMBLE TERMS: OUR REPEATED PETITIONS HAVE BEEN ANSWERED ONLY BY REPEATED INJURY.

A PRINCE, WHOSE CHARACTER IS THUS MARKED BY EVERY ACT WHICH MAY DEFINE A TYRANT, IS UNFIT TO BE THE RULER OF A FREE PEOPLE.

NOR HAVE WE BEEN WANTING IN ATTENTIONS TO OUR BRITTISH BRETHREN. WE HAVE WARNED THEM FROM TIME TO TIME OF ATTEMPTS BY THEIR LEGISLATURE TO EXTEND AN UNWARRANTABLE JURISDICTION OVER US. WE HAVE REMINDED THEM OF THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF OUR EMIGRATION AND SETTLEMENT HERE. WE HAVE APPEALED TO THEIR NATIVE JUSTICE AND MAGNANIMITY, AND WE HAVE CONJURED THEM BY THE TIES OF OUR COMMON KINDRED TO DISAVOW THESE USURPATIONS, WHICH, WOULD INEVITABLY INTERRUPT OUR CONNECTIONS AND CORRESPONDENCE. THEY TOO HAVE BEEN DEAF TO THE VOICE OF JUSTICE AND OF CONSANGUINITY. WE MUST, THEREFORE, ACQUIESCE IN THE NECESSITY, WHICH DENOUNCES OUR SEPARATION, AND HOLD THEM, AS WE HOLD THE REST OF MANKIND, ENEMIES IN WAR, IN PEACE FRIENDS.

WE, THEREFORE, THE REPRESENTATIVES OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, IN GENERAL CONGRESS, ASSEMBLED, APPEALING TO THE SUPREME JUDGE OF THE WORLD FOR THE RECTITUDE OF OUR INTENTIONS, DO, IN THE NAME, AND BY AUTHORITY OF THE GOOD PEOPLE OF THESE COLONIES, SOLEMNLY PUBLISH AND DECLARE, THAT THESE UNITED COLONIES ARE, AND OF RIGHT OUGHT TO BE FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES; THAT THEY ARE ABSOLVED FROM ALL ALLEGIANCE TO THE BRITISH CROWN, AND THAT ALL POLITICAL CONNECTION BETWEEN THEM AND THE STATE OF GREAT BRITAIN, IS AND OUGHT TO BE TOTALLY DISSOLVED; AND THAT AS FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES, THEY HAVE FULL POWER TO LEVY WAR, CONCLUDE PEACE, CONTRACT ALLIANCES, ESTABLISH COMMERCE, AND TO DO ALL OTHER ACTS AND THINGS WHICH INDEPENDENT STATES MAY OF RIGHT DO. AND FOR THE SUPPORT OF THIS DECLARATION, WITH A FIRM RELIANCE ON THE PROTECTION OF DIVINE PROVIDENCE, WE MUTUALLY PLEDGE TO EACH OTHER OUR LIVES, OUR FORTUNES AND OUR SACRED HONOR.

text:
What if the birds arriving each year had crossed more than a border?

The Book of Nut offers a startling explanation for the birds arriving in Egypt each year. It describes ba-birds entering from Nut’s northeastern and northwestern sides, then changing into ordinary birds to feed in the marshes. A ba, usually pictured as a human-headed bird, was an aspect of a person’s individuality. Here, a familiar seasonal arrival opens onto something much stranger: the sky goddess and the realm of the dead belong to the same journey as the flocks overhead. Imagine watching the first birds and wondering what they had been before they crossed the sky.

A flock could arrive from beyond the visible world. If those birds changed at Nut’s boundary, what might a person waiting in the marshes fail to recognise?

The US already approved a $2.1bn sale of 500 interceptors on Oct 30, but he says delivery could take years. Midterms are Tuesday. Whatever happens in Doha before then, you'll feel it at the pump first.
